text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH for service /v1/generate in eu-west-1 - spike in 5xx and timeouts detected by synthetic canaries.

infra-bot: Alert: 5xx-rate > 3% for 3m across multiple hosts in eu-west-1 (ASG app-eu-*)

Alice (oncall): I'm on it. seeing errors from model worker RPCs: tls handshake failures + occasional RST.

Carlos (support): We already have 4 customer reports complaining about high latency and 502s starting ~09:08 UTC. No broad billing impact yet but API errors.

Alice (oncall): Initial hypothesis: something network-y - transient connection resets. Raj, can you check any recent route/NACL/SG changes in eu-west?

Raj (net-eng): Checking infra audit - there was an automated route-propagation fix pushed to transit-gw attachments at 08:59 UTC for a peering tweak. No explicit NACL/SG changes in last 2h.

Maya (sre): tcpdump on app hosts shows lots of ICMP fragmentation-needed and packets with don't-fragment set? also MSS clamping errors on some flows.

Alice (oncall): ICMP fragmentation-needed = MTU mismatch. That would explain TLS handshake failures and RSTs (path MTU blackhole). Where are the packets being MTU-sized? NAT gateway in front of private subnets + transit gateway path to model-serving cluster.

Raj (net-eng): I see the transit-gw attachment to the model-serving VPC was changed to enable path-mtu-discovery settings during earlier fix. Looks like the TGW route advertised a lower MTU, but the NAT gateway ENI is still at 9001 and downstream host interfaces are at 1500. Strange.

Alice (oncall): Can someone run a quick mturoute / traceroute -M on a problematic host to the model backend?

Maya (sre): Ran on app-03:
```
# mturoute 10.4.8.12
start MTU 1500 -> next hop 10.4.0.1 reports need 1400
... path shows a hop in the transit-gw where DF flagged and returns ICMP need-to-frag 1400
```

Raj (net-eng): That matches: transit-gw to peered VPC path is advertising lower MTU (1400) but NAT gateway for outbound traffic is encapsulating jumbo frames (9001) causing mismatch when packets traverse the TGW. Some hosts fallback but many TLS sessions fail.

Alice (oncall): Customer impact: partial - about 12% of requests in eu-west hitting affected path return 502/504, mainly flows that cross TGW + NAT. Canary traffic hitting local AZ-only paths is fine.

Carlos (support): Noted. I'll message affected customers and escalate to enterprise reps.

Maya (sre): Mitigation options: (A) Force NAT gateway ENI to 1500 MTU (can't change MTU on AWS-managed nat gw) (B) Update host ENIs to MTU=1400 (quick but impacts local performance) (C) Rollback the transit-gw path-mtu change (if safe) (D) Add route to avoid TGW for affected subnets (surgical).

Raj (net-eng): We can quickly adjust the VPC route to prefer direct AZ-local NAT path for app ASGs (D), pushing traffic off the TGW while we fix propagation. I'll prepare a targeted route update for the affected route table (rtb-0aaffed).

Alice (oncall): Do it. Keep it targeted to eu-west-1a/b subnets only. Notify if rollback needed.

Raj (net-eng): Applying route update to rtb-0aaffed -> blackhole fallback to nat-local -> update pushed at 09:20:12 UTC

infra-bot: Route change executed: rtb-0aaffed -> 10.0.12.0/20 via nat-local (applied by raj)

Maya (sre): I'm re-running canaries now.

Alice (oncall): Observability - spike in errors dropping from 12% -> 3% over last 3m. Latency slightly higher but stable.

incident-bot: Incident severity remaining P1. oncall: Alice. Estimated affected customers: ~60 (partial).

Carlos (support): Posting customer update draft: "We saw a partial networking degradation in eu-west-1 affecting a subset of customers resulting in higher error rates. We've applied a targeted routing mitigation and are monitoring." Want to add ETA?

Emma (ops-lead): Keep ETA TBD until we validate full fix. Good to give 1-2 hour window for root cause and cross-AZ rollback.

Alice (oncall): Root cause note: transit-gw path-mtu feature change + NAT jumbo frames created intermittent fragmentation issues; path MTU discovery didn't succeed in some flows leading to blackholes. We'll plan a follow-up to reconcile TGW MTU advertisement vs NAT encapsulation.

Raj (net-eng): I'm opening a CR to ensure MTU advert and NAT behavior are aligned. For now, route change keeps traffic on local NATs. Will also check any VPC peering encap setting.

Maya (sre): CPU on app hosts rose ~8% after MTU change due to segmentation, but nothing critical. Tracking metrics and will scale ASG if needed.

Alice (oncall): Handoff plan - I'm pausing active remediation at 09:28 UTC. Emma will take the late-shift handoff at 09:35 UTC.

Emma (ops-lead): Taking handoff. Summary: partial eu-west-1 networking degradation due to MTU mismatch after TGW route change; mitigation applied via targeted route update to avoid TGW for affected subnets. Key next steps: 1) Validate route change holds for 1h, 2) coordinate net-eng CR and schedule a safe TGW rollback or MTU harmonization, 3) post-mortem.

Alice (oncall): Leaving detailed commands and artifacts:
```
# check tcpdump
sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 host 10.4.8.12 and (tcp or icmp)
# mturoute
mturoute 10.4.8.12
# route table
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids rtb-0aaffed
```

Raj (net-eng): Filed CR-4921: "Align TGW MTU advertisement with NAT and host MTUs". Links to logs and mturoute output attached in ticket.

incident-bot: Incident status: MONITORED - mitigation applied.

Carlos (support): Sent update to affected customers. No escalations yet.

Emma (ops-lead): I'll keep monitoring and will update within 30m. If errors creep >5% re-open paging.

Alice (oncall): Thanks all. I'll join follow-up postmortem.

Maya (sre): logging note: include mturoute output and tcpdump snippets in the postmortem.

Emma (ops-lead): Handoff complete 09:35 UTC.
